note: A pious man suffered from pain in his heart, and the doctors said his only cure was to drink warm milk every morning. So a goat was brought and tied to the leg of his bed, and he drank from it. When his friends came to visit and saw the goat, they exclaimed that there was an armed bandit in his house, since goats graze on neighbours' crops. They examined his conduct and found no sin in him except the goat, and on his deathbed he said the same: his only sin was keeping it against the Sages' rule.
why: A teaching says the leaders of Israel after Yosef ben Yo'ezer all had some flaw. This story is raised against it: tradition identifies such a 'pious man' as a much later Sage, yet he had no flaw but the goat.

terms.meaning: Sheep and goats. The Sages forbade raising them in settled parts of the Land of Israel because they graze on other people's fields.
A teaching from the early Sages that was not included in the Mishna, the core collection of Jewish law.
